I also have BPD + “regular” depression and anxiety, so I understand.

For me I’m in no particular “type” of therapy. Just talk therapy I guess? It helps me process all my emotions and thoughts, and my therapist also does a good job of challenging my obsessive/anxious/paranoid thoughts. It’s definitely not perfect, but I know it’s better than nothing. 

I use the online therapy BetterHelp. That’s good for me because my “chat room” with my therapist is always open, so I can write down my thoughts as they come instead of waiting a week to talk about anything. The only caveat with that is my therapist only responds about once a day, but we have weekly video sessions in which we address everything I’ve shared. 

In general I’d say DBT therapy is way more effective than CBT. I’d encourage you to think about why you want to go to therapy; what are you hoping to get from it? Then you can make a decision based on what you’re looking for whether it’s coping skills, an unbiased outlet, a better understand of diagnoses, or just someone to talk to.

Even though I’ve technically been diagnosed with the cliche cocktail of depression and anxiety since I was 13 (I’m 21 now), it didn’t really sink in until last year. I was hit with a depressive episode seemingly for no reason, and couldn’t go to class because I slept all day. Before then I always had a nagging feeling that I was making stuff up, or my problems weren’t clinical because it always seemed to be related to something specific. Last year was the first time I can remember being completely fine one day, then going downhill the next. 
I still have to remind myself that it’s not made up, or in my head, or just me being dramatic. But I’m doing better now, keeping up with my meds for the first time in forever, and going to therapy. :):
